observations.statement: Planning Wizard is specified as a finished-product workspace that accepts an Approved PRD Pack, normalized requirements input, or structured Assistant Chat seed and produces implementation-ready Plans, a Final Plan Pack, and an ApprovedPlanPack for Plan Compile only after explicit Approve And Build approval.

Planning Wizard owns the PlanningRun aggregate, topic graph and agents, topic-scoped ledger work, context capsules, conversion and audits, integration, amendments, compile readiness, ApprovedPlanPack authority, GUI states, and the approval transition, while consuming the named planning, runtime, contract, source-control, permission, GUI, orchestration, and HITL contracts and disclaiming low-level execution ownership after Executor activation.

Planning Wizard may self-initiate the enumerated web and browser operations through the shared dispatcher when external material matters to planning; resulting receipts, citations, artifacts, reasons, closure states, and failures are planning evidence that may enter planning lineage but confer no WorkNode, queue, code, build-task, or Plan Compile authority.

PWIZ-001 retires Chain Wizard and Plan Wizard from active terminology, defines exactly three canonical seed families, requires preservation of provenance and project/work-intent context, permits overlapping compatible intents, requires a bounded structured Assistant Chat handoff, and permits a traceable fast path when chat already contains sufficient intake intent.

PWIZ-001 acceptance explicitly requires source-atom fidelity, preservation of exact tokens and corrections, non-creation of executable or governance artifacts by this compile, and preservation of seed identity, version or hash, warnings, lineage, project context, and compatible work-intent axes; its listed validation surfaces are the plan-index and bootstrap-ledger validators.

The approval repair addendum is expressly planning-only and does not itself create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, queues, implementation files, runtime dispatch, generated governance artifacts, or a governance seal.
The production final-review control dispatches cmd.planning_wizard.approve_and_build with the enumerated displayed CAS/currentness values, approval actor, and deterministic idempotency key.

Approval fails closed if any listed planning or displayed review input changed after review; stale approval must route to bounded revalidation or review refresh and cannot silently approve a different plan.

Successful approval is specified to atomically write approval_cas_receipt, publish PlanApproved, create or bind exactly one PlanCompileRun, and synchronously return its durable identifier; eventual projection is allowed only for the pending shell, and identical CAS inputs plus idempotency key must return the same run.

Planning Wizard delegates execution_unit_context to the Executor-owned contract, forbids a local field-list copy, requires schema_version for embedded persisted context, and forbids secrets and credentials in that payload.

Persisted approval and final-review events must consume the canonical EventRecord envelope; Planning Wizard owns approval CAS and idempotency behavior but EventRecord conformance does not grant authority to emit Plan Compile runtime artifacts.

The GUI and concept surface must not expose START, BUILD, Start Chain, or Approve & Continue as ordinary launch controls; Approve And Build is the sole ordinary final-planning launch authority, and later controls require scoped commands, disabled reasons, receipt effects, and stale-projection behavior.

PWIZ-002 models each topic, integration pass, and attached audit or repair as a bounded child thread under one Planning Run; PlanningRun owns the listed aggregate state and separates project context from one or more compatible work-intent axes.

PWIZ-003 requires an evidence-driven dynamic topic graph, supports add, split, merge, rename, defer, reopen, reorder, and impact operations with recorded rationale and invalidations, and requires GUI guidance without preventing dependency-safe navigation or parallel background work.

PWIZ-004 requires every substantive exchange to append an event and synchronize topic and affected global planning state before the turn completes, supplies each fresh bounded topic agent with a bounded context capsule and write card, and constrains questions to active-topic implementation-readiness gaps.

PWIZ-004 assigns the controller proactive coverage of behavior, state, data, identity, permissions, failures, edge cases, integration, acceptance evidence, currentness, idempotency, migration, operations, and implementation boundaries, while limiting user questions to named genuine decision or authority classes.

Context-only text immediately after the core introduces one shared Planning Run ledger, typed invalidation propagation, named stale and recompile or reaudit states, amendment classifications, and immutability of Approved PRD Packs; this observation is not used to substantiate a core finding.

candidate_findings.title: Canonical seed families lack a typed intake and rejection contract
candidate_findings.statement: The core names exactly three seed families and a set of fields to preserve, but it does not define a discriminator, required versus optional fields, field types, normalization precedence, version compatibility, duplicate or conflicting-source handling, or outcomes for malformed, unknown, or stale seeds.
candidate_findings.impact: Independent builders can accept different payloads or silently normalize away provenance, producing incompatible PlanningRun intake and inconsistent readiness.

candidate_findings.title: Self-initiated research has no bounded lifecycle contract
candidate_findings.statement: The research clause uses the judgment trigger materially changes planning and names evidence and failure artifacts, but does not specify authorization checks, budgets or limits, source-currentness thresholds, cancellation, timeout, retry, deduplication, closure criteria, or the terminal behavior of failed research.
candidate_findings.impact: Equivalent planning inputs can cause unbounded or inconsistent external operations and leave builders unable to decide when research is sufficient or safely closed.

candidate_findings.title: Approval payload is enumerated but not typed or canonically encoded
candidate_findings.statement: The final-review command lists CAS values and an idempotency key without defining requiredness, scalar and hash types, canonical serialization, hash encoding or algorithm, nullability, revision domains, actor representation, or deterministic key derivation.
candidate_findings.impact: GUI, command, and backend implementations can compute non-equivalent currentness or idempotency inputs and either reject valid approval or approve stale state.

candidate_findings.title: Stale approval recovery is not deterministic
candidate_findings.statement: The core requires fail-closed behavior and names bounded revalidation or final-review refresh, but does not define a stale error code or receipt, route-selection rules, the bound, which values are refreshed, user-visible state, cancellation and retry behavior, or a terminal outcome after repeated staleness.
candidate_findings.impact: Clients can diverge after the same stale CAS failure, strand approval, or conceal why review must be repeated.

candidate_findings.title: Atomic approval side effects lack a transaction and recovery protocol
candidate_findings.statement: The requirement says receipt write, event publication, and PlanCompileRun creation or binding are atomic, but it does not define ordering, commit point, transactional boundary across stores, outbox or equivalent publication rule, rollback, crash recovery, or reconciliation for partial success.
candidate_findings.impact: A failure between side effects can produce an approval without a run, a run without durable approval evidence, or duplicate publication at the planning-to-compile authority boundary.

candidate_findings.title: Idempotency covers only the identical-delivery case
candidate_findings.statement: Returning the same run is defined only for duplicate delivery with the same CAS inputs and idempotency key; behavior is absent for a reused key with different inputs, simultaneous approvals with different keys, actor changes, an already-bound run, timeout before response, and retry after an ambiguous commit.
candidate_findings.impact: Concurrent or ambiguous approval delivery can create competing run identities or inconsistent receipts despite the exactly-one promise.

candidate_findings.title: Final-review GUI truth and accessibility are not acceptance-testable
candidate_findings.statement: The core names displayed CAS values, a pending launch shell, prohibited control labels, disabled reasons, receipts, and stale behavior, but does not specify which technical values are visibly rendered versus internally bound, redaction and formatting, confirmation and cancellation, loading and error presentation, keyboard or focus behavior, accessibility names, or projection-timeout behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: A backend-conformant implementation can still present misleading approval state or an inaccessible launch control with no shared GUI oracle.

candidate_findings.title: PlanningRun lacks a normative lifecycle state machine
candidate_findings.statement: PlanningRun is assigned status, hashes, threads, drafts, amendments, invalidations, audit cycles, final pack, and handoff events, but the core does not define status values, legal transitions, invariants among those fields, creation and resume semantics, cancellation, archival, retry, persistence, or concurrent update rules.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can implement incompatible aggregate lifecycles and permit final approval while topics, audits, hashes, or handoff state disagree.

candidate_findings.title: Topic graph mutations lack preconditions and conflict semantics
candidate_findings.statement: The core names add, split, merge, rename, defer, reopen, reorder, and impact operations plus recorded reasons and invalidations, but does not define command payloads, identity retention, graph invariants, dependency-cycle handling, atomicity, version or CAS checks, concurrent-edit resolution, rejection reasons, or deterministic invalidation propagation.
candidate_findings.impact: Parallel topic work can corrupt the graph, lose lineage, or invalidate different drafts for the same mutation.

candidate_findings.title: Per-turn durable synchronization has no atomicity or recovery semantics
candidate_findings.statement: Every substantive exchange must append an event and update topic and global state before completion, and unsynchronized chat state must not advance a topic, but substantive exchange, completion, acknowledgement, update ordering, atomicity, duplicate-event idempotency, concurrent topic-agent writes, rollback, and crash recovery are undefined.
candidate_findings.impact: A partial or repeated turn can leave event history and planning projections divergent while different implementations disagree whether the topic may advance.

candidate_findings.title: Planning Context Capsule lacks identity, currentness, and protection semantics
candidate_findings.statement: The core lists capsule contents and calls the capsule bounded, but does not define a schema or version, capsule identity and hash, size or token bound, source-currentness snapshot, redaction and authorization, refresh or invalidation triggers, or required behavior when referenced artifacts are unavailable.
candidate_findings.impact: Fresh agents can receive stale, oversized, or differently filtered context and produce non-reproducible topic plans or expose restricted material.

candidate_findings.title: Safe-autonomy classification lacks a deterministic decision oracle
candidate_findings.statement: The controller may auto-resolve from evidence, apply safe defaults, defer downstream details, and ask only for named classes of user direction, but the core does not define evidence sufficiency, what qualifies as safe, risk thresholds, the recorded-assumption shape, escalation precedence when categories overlap, or correction behavior after a default is invalidated.
candidate_findings.impact: Agents can make materially different product decisions from the same evidence or incorrectly suppress required HITL.

candidate_findings.title: PlanUnit acceptance surfaces do not prove the specified product behavior
candidate_findings.statement: The PlanUnits in the core repeat lineage-fidelity and non-generation checks and list only plan-index and bootstrap-ledger validators; they provide no executable acceptance oracle for intake validation, approval CAS and idempotency, stale failure, PlanningRun transitions, topic mutation, durable synchronization, GUI state, or accessibility.
candidate_findings.impact: The declared validation surfaces can pass while consequential runtime and GUI behavior remains absent or mutually incompatible.

candidate_findings.title: Machine-readable PlanUnit dependencies are empty despite stated contract dependencies
candidate_findings.statement: The document declares many consumed systems and external SSOT contracts, while each visible PlanUnit has empty depends_on and unblocks lists; the core does not explain whether or how those stated dependencies enter compile ordering and readiness.
candidate_findings.impact: Automated dependency analysis can treat these PlanUnits as isolated and schedule or approve them before required contracts are available.

candidate_findings.title: PWIZ-004 GUI classification may exclude user-facing conversation behavior
candidate_findings.statement: PWIZ-004 describes topic conversations and user questions but marks gui_related false and characterizes the requirement as non-visual backend or workflow behavior; no split identifies which user-visible states belong to a GUI owner.
candidate_findings.impact: GUI and accessibility assurance can omit question, decision, synchronization, and error states that users must interact with.

candidate_findings.title: Topic operation identifiers are preserved without command or event contracts
candidate_findings.statement: PWIZ-003 preserves add_topic, split_topic, merge_topics, and mark_topic_impacted tokens, while the canonical behavior only names generic controller verbs and provides no mapping to scoped commands, events, payloads, receipts, or errors.
candidate_findings.impact: Controller, GUI, and event consumers can use incompatible operation names and payload semantics despite token preservation.

candidate_findings.title: Implementation-ready and compile-readiness thresholds are undefined in the core
candidate_findings.statement: The scope promises implementation-ready Plans and ownership assigns compile readiness, but the visible acceptance criteria primarily prove compilation lineage and non-generation; no required completeness dimensions, blocking severity threshold, or readiness receipt is defined.
candidate_findings.impact: The same plan content can be deemed ready by one builder and incomplete by another before approval.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Input-family cardinality and canonical identifiers are explicit: ApprovedPRDPack, normalized_requirements_pack, and assistant_chat_handoff_seed.
External research artifacts are explicitly planning evidence only and cannot independently create execution artifacts or Plan Compile authority.
Stale approval is explicitly fail-closed and cannot silently approve a plan different from the one reviewed.
The happy-path approval contract explicitly requires exactly one PlanCompileRun, synchronous return of its durable identifier, and replay identity for the same CAS inputs and idempotency key.
execution_unit_context ownership, schema-version presence for an embedded persisted payload, and secret-exclusion constraints are explicit.
The canonical EventRecord envelope is explicitly required for persisted approval and final-review events, and schema conformance is explicitly denied as independent runtime-artifact authority.
Ordinary GUI launch authority and prohibited legacy or ambiguous control labels are explicit.
Project context and work intent are explicitly independent, and more than one compatible delivery intent may coexist.
The topic taxonomy is explicitly evidence-driven rather than universal, and the negative constraint forbids hardcoding one taxonomy for all projects.
The core explicitly forbids advancing from chat state that has not been durably synchronized, generic irrelevant questions, and conversion of ordinary uncertainty into a user-decision blocker.
The Assistant Chat handoff is explicitly structured and bounded rather than an unbounded raw transcript, and the raw transcript cannot be the sole handoff.

Each visible PlanUnit explicitly states that this compile creates no WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, GoalRuns, implementation files, generated governance artifacts, or production build tasks.

unknowns.statement: The detailed semantics of the consumed PRD Builder, Assistant Chat, Goal Runtime, Plan Document System, Plan To Node Compilation, testing, Executor, permissions, GUI, Orchestrator, and HITL contracts are unknown because those documents are outside this blind window.
The field sets and validation behavior of the Executor-owned execution_unit_context and canonical EventRecord schemas are unknown in this assignment.
The concrete schemas and producers of ApprovedPRDPack, normalized_requirements_pack, and assistant_chat_handoff_seed are unknown within the assigned text.
The exact checks performed by the plan-index and bootstrap-ledger validators are unknown because only their command names appear in the core.
The referenced source atoms, source shards, decisions, and corrections were not inspected under the blind-scope rule, so their content and completeness relative to these PlanUnits are unknown.
The broader PlanCompileRun lifecycle and downstream meaning of PlanApproved are unknown beyond the approval boundary stated in the core.
The status values named as PlanningRun-owned state are not enumerated in the core.

Context-only line 361 supplies additional invalidation and amendment behavior, but the remainder of PWIZ-005 lies outside the assigned context range and its full contract cannot be assessed or used as a core finding.

exact_evidence_refs.exact_quote: Planning Wizard is the finished-product planning workspace that consumes an Approved PRD Pack, normalized requirements input, or structured Assistant Chat seed and turns it into implementation-ready Plans, a Final Plan Pack, and an ApprovedPlanPack suitable for Plan Compile after explicit `Approve And Build` approval.

Planning Wizard owns PlanningRun, topic graph, topic agents, topic-scoped ledger work, Planning Context Capsules, topic conversion and audits, final integration, Planning Amendments, compile readiness, ApprovedPlanPack authority, Planning Wizard GUI states, and the Approve And Build transition. It consumes PRD Builder, Assistant Chat, Goal Runtime, Plan Document System, Plan To Node Compilation, Automated Testing, Executor, Contracts, source-control, permissions, Final GUI, Orchestrator, and HITL contracts without owning low-level runtime execution after Executor activation.

Planning Wizard may self-initiate web/search/fetch/extract/research/deep-research/crawl/map (`websearch`, `webfetch`, `webextract`, `webresearch`, `webcrawl`, `webmap`) and Site Reader/browser evidence through the shared PM WebOperation/BrowserAction dispatcher when current external facts, docs, issues, PRs, URLs, visual/dynamic pages, project context, comparative research, or source authority materially changes planning. The resulting read receipts, extract receipts, citations, browser artifacts, source-selection reasons, research closure states, and failure states are planning evidence only until explicit approval; they may flow into Planning Context Capsules, topic ledgers, topic plans, audit findings, Final Plan Pack source refs, and ApprovedPlanPack lineage, but they do not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, runtime code, implementation files, production build tasks, or Plan Compile authority by themselves. Retired Chain Wizard wording remains compatibility/search lineage only and does not become a dependency or product term.

canonical_text: 'The canonical product name is Planning Wizard; Chain Wizard and Plan Wizard are stale names that must be retired from active product prose, UI, commands, events, and contracts. Planning Wizard accepts exactly three canonical input seed families before topic work begins: ApprovedPRDPack, normalized_requirements_pack, or assistant_chat_handoff_seed. Each seed preserves source identity, version, hashes, warnings, amendments, lineage, project context, and bounded work_intent axes; multiple compatible intents such as feature work plus release PR delivery may overlap in one PlanningRun without collapsing project context into a single lossy mode enum. Send to Planning Wizard creates a structured seed containing goal, scope, project, requirements, assumptions, open questions, source message references, artifacts, repository context, and suggested mode rather than copying an unbounded transcript. When Assistant Chat already contains sufficient planning-intake intent, the handoff may construct a traceable seed or draft PRD Pack and begin Planning Wizard intake without forcing the user through repeated PRD Builder questions.'

negative_constraints:
- Do not use Chain Wizard or Plan Wizard as current terminology.
- Do not use the raw Assistant Chat transcript as the sole Planning Wizard handoff.
- Do not sacrifice provenance, quality warnings, or readiness validation to avoid repetition.
- Do not collapse overlapping compatible work intents or project context into a single lossy mode enum.

This addendum closes the Approve And Build defects from the PMConcept readiness report. It does not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, implementation files, runtime dispatch, generated governance artifacts, or a governance seal.

The production final-review control dispatches `cmd.planning_wizard.approve_and_build`. The command payload carries the exact final-review CAS/currentness values shown to the user: `project_id`, `planning_run_id`, PlanningRun revision, topic map version, `approved_plan_pack_id`, pack version/hash, project-context snapshot hash, PlanUnit index hash, acceptance-unit index hash, testing policy hash, final audit/closure hash, approval actor, and deterministic idempotency key.

Approval fails closed when any planning state, source pack, project context, topic readiness, audit closure, testing policy, Plan index input, or displayed final-review CAS input changed after the user reviewed it. A stale failure routes to bounded revalidation or final-review refresh; it must not silently approve a different plan.

Successful approval atomically writes `approval_cas_receipt`, publishes `PlanApproved`, creates or binds exactly one `PlanCompileRun`, and returns the durable `plan_compile_run_id` synchronously. Projection reconciliation may show a pending launch shell in Orchestrator Plan Compile, but run identity itself may not be left to eventual projection. Duplicate delivery with the same CAS inputs and idempotency key returns the same `PlanCompileRun`.

Planning Wizard and PlanApproved records consume `execution_unit_context` only through the Executor-owned contract in `Plans/Executor_Protocol.md` and `Plans/execution_unit_context.schema.json`. They must not define a local context field list, must not persist an embedded context payload without `schema_version`, and must not store secrets, tokens, passwords, credentials, API keys, provider auth values, or local machine secrets in the context payload.

Persisted Planning Wizard approval, PlanApproved, and final-review events consume the canonical EventRecord envelope in `Plans/Contracts_V0.md#EventRecord` and `Plans/event_record.schema.json`. Planning Wizard owns approval behavior and CAS/idempotency semantics, but it must not copy the EventRecord field set or treat the EventRecord schema as permission to emit PlanCompile runtime artifacts.

The Planning Wizard and PMConcept concept surface must not expose `START`, `BUILD`, `Start Chain`, or `Approve & Continue` as ordinary build-launch controls. `Approve And Build` is the only ordinary final planning approval-to-PlanCompileRun launch authority; later controls are post-approval Plan Compile or runtime controls with scoped commands, disabled reasons, receipt effects, and stale-projection behavior.

canonical_text: 'Each planning topic, integration pass, and attached audit/repair activity is a bounded child thread grouped by planning_run_id and thread_group_id under one collapsible Planning Run parent. PlanningRun owns source pack identity, project and work-intent context, thread group, global planning ledger, dynamic topic map, topic threads, topic plan drafts, amendments, invalidations, audit cycles, final plan pack, status, hashes, and handoff events. Planning Wizard classifies project context independently from work intent so overlapping cases such as an existing Git repository plus feature work plus PR delivery are represented without a misleading single mode enum. Project context supports greenfield, existing local project, existing Git repository, remote SSH project, and fork or external upstream contexts, with explicit repository and host facts. Work intent supports new product, feature or enhancement, refactor or rewrite,
  bugfix or bounded task, and contribution PR, and may include more than one compatible delivery intent.'
